about.title: Half Moon Bay Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Half Moon Bay's mix of coastal highway traffic and local commuter routes makes for a particular kind of driving environment. Rt 1, SR-1, N Cabrillo Highway, and San Mateo Road carry a steady flow of vehicles, tourists, and farm trucks alike, and public crash records show 32 injury collisions and 45 injured people in the most recent final year on file. Sunday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. show up more often than other times, which tracks with weekend traffic heading back toward the peninsula. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, LawProactive can connect you, free of charge, with an independent personal injury attorney familiar with San Mateo County claims. The attorney works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. Every case is different, so the first step is simply getting the right person looking at yours.
commonInjuries: Deep lacerations requiring stitches or surgery

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls Back

items.title: California's Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a claim, but if a government entity (like Caltrans, for a road issue) may be involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Getting evidence preserved early, skid marks, signal timing, dashcam footage, matters before it disappears.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Cut Both Ways
items.desc: California allows recovery even if you're partly at fault, but your percentage of fault reduces what you can recover. An attorney can push back against an insurer trying to inflate your share of blame in a two-lane highway crash on Route 1.

items.title: No Cap Means No Reason to Rush a Settlement
items.desc: California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so there's little upside to accepting a fast, low offer from the other driver's insurer. Skipping a recorded statement until you've talked to someone protects you from having your own words used against you later.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's best to avoid it until you've spoken with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can shrink or shift blame, and anything you say can be used later. An independent attorney can handle those conversations on your behalf.

items.question: What if my accident happened on Highway 1 near Half Moon Bay and involved a road hazard?
items.answer: Claims involving state highways or road design issues can sometimes name a government entity, like Caltrans, as a defendant. Those claims carry a much shorter filing deadline, sometimes just six months, so it's important to get evidence and photos documented quickly. An attorney can help sort out whether that applies to your situation.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and the attorneys in the network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost or obligation to move forward.
